scenes.tts: Your brain is about two percent of your weight, but it uses about twenty percent of your resting energy. Who delivers fuel to the far end of an axon?
scenes.caption: Your brain is about 2 percent of your weight, but it uses about 20 percent of your resting energy. Who delivers fuel to the far end of an axon?
scenes.visual: Title card: Who Feeds the Far End? Then a body silhouette with the brain highlighted, beside two bars: 2 percent of body mass, 20 percent of resting energy. Zoom to one neuron whose axon runs off screen, a question mark at its far end.
scenes.narration: Your brain is about 2 percent of your weight, but it uses about 20 percent of your resting energy. Who delivers fuel to the far end of an axon?

scenes.tts: Start with the cost. After every impulse, the sodium potassium pump puts sodium and potassium back. Each cycle spends one A T P.
scenes.caption: Start with the cost. After every impulse, the sodium-potassium pump puts sodium and potassium back. Each cycle spends one ATP.
scenes.visual: Label: 1. Cost. A patch of axon membrane: sodium flows in and potassium out as a spike passes, then the Na+/K+-ATPase cycles. Counter on screen: 3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in, 1 ATP.
scenes.narration: Start with the cost. After every impulse, the sodium-potassium pump puts sodium and potassium back. Each cycle spends one ATP.

scenes.tts: In rodent grey matter, most of the energy used for signaling goes to these pumps.
scenes.caption: In rodent grey matter, most of the energy used for signalling goes to these pumps.
scenes.visual: A grey-matter energy budget bar with the pump share highlighted. Credit: Attwell and Laughlin, 2001, and later revisions.
scenes.narration: In rodent grey matter, most of the energy used for signalling goes to these pumps.

scenes.tts: Now the distance. A motor axon can run from your spinal cord to your foot, about a meter.
scenes.caption: Now the distance. A motor axon can run from your spinal cord to your foot, about a metre.
scenes.visual: Label: 2. Distance. A leg silhouette with one motor axon drawn to scale from the spinal cord to the foot. Ruler: about 1 metre.
scenes.narration: Now the distance. A motor axon can run from your spinal cord to your foot, about a metre.

scenes.tts: The cell body is full of mitochondria. Could it just make A T P and let it diffuse down the axon?
scenes.caption: The cell body is full of mitochondria. Could it just make ATP and let it diffuse down the axon?
scenes.visual: The soma packed with mitochondria; ATP gathers at the start of the axon. Pause and predict card: diffuse all the way?
scenes.narration: The cell body is full of mitochondria. Could it just make ATP and let it diffuse down the axon?

scenes.tts: Over a micrometer, A T P spreads in milliseconds. Over a millimeter, it takes about half an hour to an hour.
scenes.caption: Over a micrometre, ATP spreads in milliseconds. Over a millimetre, it takes about half an hour to an hour.
scenes.visual: A diffusion clock. Rows: 1 micrometre, a few milliseconds; 1 millimetre, about half an hour to an hour. Note: time grows with the square of the distance.
scenes.narration: Over a micrometre, ATP spreads in milliseconds. Over a millimetre, it takes about half an hour to an hour.

scenes.tts: Over a meter, it would take fifty to a hundred years.
scenes.caption: Over a metre, it would take 50 to 100 years.
scenes.visual: The clock adds rows: 1 centimetre, about 2 to 4 days; 1 metre, about 50 to 100 years. The last row is highlighted.
scenes.narration: Over a metre, it would take 50 to 100 years.

scenes.tts: So the axon must make its A T P locally, in its own mitochondria and by its own glycolysis.
scenes.caption: So the axon must make its ATP locally, in its own mitochondria and by its own glycolysis.
scenes.visual: Mitochondria spaced along the axon light up; small glycolysis icons glow in the axon's cytoplasm. Label: made locally.
scenes.narration: So the axon must make its ATP locally, in its own mitochondria and by its own glycolysis.

scenes.tts: Then the cover. Along a myelinated stretch in the brain and spinal cord, myelin covers about ninety eight to ninety nine percent.
scenes.caption: Then the cover. Along a myelinated stretch in the brain and spinal cord, myelin covers about 98 to 99 percent.
scenes.visual: Label: 3. Cover. Myelin segments slide on one by one, leaving short glowing nodes. A coverage meter fills to 98 to 99 percent, labelled: one myelinated stretch; real axons vary. Scale: node about 1 micrometre; internode about 50 to 100 micrometres.
scenes.narration: Then the cover. Along a myelinated stretch in the brain and spinal cord, myelin covers about 98 to 99 percent.

scenes.tts: The bare gaps between segments are the nodes. The axon meets the fluid outside mainly there. Myelin is not a seal, but it limits the axon's access to glucose.
scenes.visual: Close-up of a node: exposed axon membrane between two sheaths, a thin space under each sheath. Caption: the axon's membrane meets the fluid outside mainly at the node; a thin space under each sheath remains. Label: limits, not seals.
scenes.narration: The bare gaps between segments are the nodes. The axon meets the fluid outside mainly there. Myelin is not a seal, but it limits the axon's access to glucose.

scenes.tts: Along each stretch, the cell touching the axon is the cell that made its myelin.
scenes.visual: Pull back: each myelin segment is revealed as part of a glial cell sitting beside the axon.
scenes.narration: Along each stretch, the cell touching the axon is the cell that made its myelin.

scenes.tts: Each segment is a sheet of one glial cell's membrane, wound around the axon.
scenes.visual: A glial cell's membrane sheet winds around the axon; a strand of cytoplasm links the cell body to the wrap.
scenes.narration: Each segment is a sheet of one glial cell's membrane, wound around the axon.

scenes.tts: One oligodendrocyte makes segments on many axons. A myelinating Schwann cell makes just one.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left, labelled CNS: one oligodendrocyte with arms to segments on several axons. Right, labelled PNS: one Schwann cell, one segment.
scenes.narration: One oligodendrocyte makes segments on many axons. A myelinating Schwann cell makes just one.

scenes.tts: That is the one idea of this lesson. Whoever wraps the axon helps feed it.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: Whoever wraps the axon helps feed it.
scenes.narration: That is the one idea of this lesson. Whoever wraps the axon helps feed it.

scenes.tts: An oligodendrocyte that has made its myelin can live on glycolysis. The evidence fits it passing lactate or pyruvate to the axon. When it loses M C T one, the transporter thought to carry that fuel out, axons degenerate as mice age.
scenes.visual: A glial cell runs glycolysis; a dashed arrow labelled inferred carries lactate and pyruvate from the wrap into the axon. In the axon's cytoplasm, lactate becomes pyruvate (label: LDH), and pyruvate enters a mitochondrion. A timeline from young to old: with glial MCT1 removed, the axon degenerates late.
scenes.narration: An oligodendrocyte that has made its myelin can live on glycolysis. The evidence fits it passing lactate or pyruvate to the axon. When it loses MCT1, the transporter thought to carry that fuel out, axons degenerate as mice age.
scenes.caption: An oligodendrocyte that has made its myelin can live on glycolysis. The evidence fits it passing lactate or pyruvate to the axon. When it loses MCT1, the transporter thought to carry that fuel out, axons degenerate as mice age.

scenes.tts: The rule has limits. The evidence is clearest for oligodendrocytes and for long-term upkeep. The experiments do not measure each impulse, and do not rule out help there. And it is help, not the only supply.
scenes.visual: Scope card, three lines: myelinating glia, oligodendrocytes that have made their myelin most clearly; long-term upkeep, each action potential not measured or ruled out; help, not sole supply. The axon also takes in glucose at a node.
scenes.narration: The rule has limits. The evidence is clearest for oligodendrocytes and for long-term upkeep. The experiments do not measure each impulse, and do not rule out help there. And it is help, not the only supply.

scenes.tts: So keep three facts together. The pumps keep spending. The cell body is far away. Myelin covers almost all of a myelinated stretch. The wrapping cell is placed to help.
scenes.visual: Three icons in a row: pump, ruler, myelin wrap. Then the takeaway card: the cell that wraps the axon is placed to help feed it.
scenes.narration: So keep three facts together. The pumps keep spending. The cell body is far away. Myelin covers almost all of a myelinated stretch. The wrapping cell is placed to help.
